open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case input set
open_points.text: “input values by port, optional expected outputs” and “Fit in port name order — presence, carriage, schema, size” do not say whether extra input names are refused or whether present expected outputs must contain every output port.
open_points.question: Must authored trial inputs exactly match all contract input ports, and, when expected outputs are present, must they exactly match all contract output ports?
options: Require exactly all declared ports and no extras for both inputs and present expected outputs
Require exact inputs but allow expected outputs for only a subset of output ports
Ignore extra names or permit missing declared ports
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly all input ports and, when expected outputs are present, exactly all output ports, with no extras.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file fixtures
open_points.text: The operation takes “input values by port, optional expected outputs,” although TrialCase permits file fixtures and the text never says what file content or file facts this operation receives.
open_points.question: What does add_trial_case receive for a one or many file port, and which layer computes and verifies its digest, size and media type?
options: Receive file bytes plus the declared media type
Receive bytes together with caller-supplied digest, size and media type
Receive an existing StoredValue file-fixture reference
open_points.default_guess: Receive file bytes by port, derive digest and size in the kernel, and take media type from the port.

open_points.subject: flows.compose_flow_version constants
open_points.text: Inputs name “constants with declared classes,” but Enforces says “A constant's StoredValue takes the value_schema and class the composing agent declared with it.”
open_points.question: Where is each constant's declared value_schema supplied, and is it an explicit part of the composition request and flow-version identity?
options: Each constant explicitly supplies value_schema and disclosure_class
The constant uses its target port's schema and supplies only disclosure_class
The kernel infers a schema from the literal value
open_points.default_guess: Require every constant to supply both value_schema and disclosure_class explicitly.

open_points.subject: effects.reach_operation_element inputs
open_points.text: The operation receives “the input values by port,” while EffectAttempt.inputs and NodeExecution.inputs must contain StoredValue and SpooledFile references, and approval previews must expose file digest, size, media type and identity.
open_points.question: Does the call receive payloads, record references and file facts together, and what exact input representation must effects preserve in approvals, attempts and trace records?
options: Pass record references plus resolved value/file bytes and facts
Pass only record references and let effects read all payloads
Pass only payloads and let effects reconstruct or look up references
open_points.default_guess: Pass the canonical record references together with the resolved payloads needed to build the request.

open_points.subject: effects.decide_effect_approval refusal trace
open_points.text: Its inputs are only “An approval identity, approve or refuse, the actor (the owner); from runs that the run has not ended,” but refusing must write a NodeExecution whose inputs are references to the element's StoredValues and SpooledFiles.
open_points.question: From where does decide_effect_approval obtain the exact input references for the refused_by_owner NodeExecution?
options: EffectApproval stores the complete input references
runs passes the element's input references to decide_effect_approval
effects reconstructs them from other run records
open_points.default_guess: Store the complete input references in EffectApproval and use those when recording refusal.

open_points.subject: Manifest JSON parsing
open_points.text: A proposal is refused when the service record “is not valid JSON,” but content identities require canonical JSON and the text does not state how duplicate object member names in a manifest are handled.
open_points.question: Are duplicate JSON member names in the service record or capability entry rejected, or does a parser choose one occurrence?
options: Reject any duplicate object member name as a manifest mismatch
Keep the first occurrence
Keep the last occurrence

open_points.subject: api_base_url validation and joining
open_points.text: An instance address is accepted when it is “an absolute http or https URL with a host,” and the request URL is “the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path.” The text does not constrain user-info, query, fragment or an existing base path, nor fully define the Host authority for them.
open_points.question: Which additional components may api_base_url contain, and exactly how are its path and authority combined with the operation path and Host header?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, with no user-info, query, fragment or base path
Allow a base path but reject user-info, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL with a host and use literal string concatenation
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, host, optional port and an optional base path; reject user-info, query and fragment, and derive Host from the parsed authority.

open_points.subject: content-addressed byte publication
open_points.text: store.put_value_bytes says “equal bytes are stored once” and “a completed file is never overwritten,” but gives no result when the expected digest already names completed, different bytes.
open_points.question: What must put_value_bytes do if an existing object has the supplied digest and size but its bytes differ?
options: Return internal_error and preserve the existing object
Return refused and preserve the existing object
Assume SHA-256 collisions cannot occur and return the existing object without comparing bytes
open_points.default_guess: Verify existing bytes and return internal_error without overwriting on any mismatch.

open_points.subject: internal_error process lifecycle
open_points.text: State 3 says “every failure it answers internal_error ... is answered first, and then surface.serve_kernel ends the process,” while State 5 only says surface “answers without detail” for an internal error and explicitly says the process ends for stop_required.
open_points.question: After an ordinary request-level internal_error, must the kernel terminate after sending the response, or continue serving?
options: Terminate after every internal_error except ignored spool-removal failures
Continue serving after ordinary internal_error and terminate only for stop_required
Terminate only for store failures that may leave a run status behind
open_points.default_guess: Terminate after every surfaced internal_error, except the explicitly ignored spool-removal failure.

open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_approval observable effect
open_points.text: It states “An approved effect is sent in this request,” but A10 permits the rebuilt request to differ or a pre-send check to fail, in which cases nothing is sent and the approval remains unused.
open_points.question: What outcome does continue_after_approval promise when approval succeeds but the effect cannot be sent under that approval?
options: Return the run waiting on a new approval or concluded operation_failed, with no send
Treat inability to send as a refusal of continue_after_approval
Guarantee the originally approved request is sent without rebuilding or repeating pre-send checks
open_points.default_guess: Return the resulting run: either waiting for a new approval or with operation_failed, without promising a send.

open_points.subject: runs.resume_run observable effect
open_points.text: It says “Elements waiting on an unreachable service are sent again,” while A14 says a revoked grant can make an element wait for approval and A09 pre-send checks can conclude operation_failed without sending.
open_points.question: Does resume promise a resend, or only that each service_unreachable element is reached again and may send, wait for approval or fail pre-send checks?
options: Reach every such element again without guaranteeing a send
Refuse the whole resume unless every element can be sent
Send using the authority valid at the original attempt regardless of later revocation or request changes
open_points.default_guess: Reach every waiting element again without guaranteeing that an HTTP request is sent.

open_points.subject: standing grant coverage
open_points.text: grant_standing_approval says “Later sends of that node in runs of that version need no approval,” while A10 and A11 require a fresh approval for every resend after an unknown attempt is resolved not_applied, even when a grant is active.
open_points.question: Must the operation's stated effect explicitly exclude resends after not_applied?
options: Yes; grants cover only sends that are not resends after not_applied
No; a grant covers every later send
A grant is automatically suspended or revoked after not_applied
open_points.default_guess: Exclude resends after not_applied from grant coverage.

open_points.subject: try_implementation observable effect
open_points.text: Its “Observable effect” is “None,” but its State impact is “One record_trial_execution per case.”
open_points.question: Does Observable effect mean no external business effect, or is the durable creation of TrialExecution records intended to be observable?
options: It means no external business effect; TrialExecution persistence remains observable kernel state
It means no persistent effect, contradicting State impact
TrialExecution records are temporary and should not be persisted
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as no external business effect while retaining the durable TrialExecution records.

open_points.subject: effects.resolve_unknown_outcome observable effect
open_points.text: Its “Observable effect” is “None,” while its State impact is “resolve_attempt” and its output is the attempt resolved.
open_points.question: Is updating the durable EffectAttempt considered an observable effect of the operation?
options: Yes; the operation observably changes the attempt while causing no service call
No; the state update should be treated as non-observable bookkeeping
The resolution should not be persisted
open_points.default_guess: Treat the durable attempt resolution as an observable kernel-state effect and state separately that no service request is made.

open_points.subject: effects.recover_in_flight_attempts observable effect
open_points.text: Its “Observable effect” is “None,” but it turns attempts unknown, may create NodeExecutions and may mark approvals used through recover_in_flight.
open_points.question: What does Observable effect mean for startup recovery, and are all of these durable changes part of the operation's promised effect?
options: All listed record changes are observable kernel-state effects; no service call is made
The changes are implementation-only and not part of the operation contract
Recovery should report the changed records as output
open_points.default_guess: Treat all listed record changes as promised durable effects and specify only that recovery performs no service call.
